reasoning: This is a close call. Set A wins narrowly on structure; content ties at 3.8. Set B has the deeper RL design. It builds each stage as a ladder of runs (table-based Q-learning, then DQN, then a full-grid CNN with ablations; REINFORCE then PPO, from one fish to a school with limited sight; fixed opponents, then naive co-learning, then an opponent pool). Its golden cases are hand-computed (Q-update 0.009, GAE 1.3775, clipped objective, exact tank geometry), and its context packets are very complete. But its brief is stale: success is defined only for Snake, and 'Not doing: Designing future environments now' sits beside two fully specced idea docs. It has one milestone per stage, and S1's M1 is very large (tabular, DQN, CNN, three ablations, library reference and replay) and ends in a single 'S' system task that has to train every rung, ablation and reference for 5 seeds. Its PL-01 is a 16-step table that mixes the environments, agents and baselines of all three stages. Set A follows the ground truth more closely. Its brief names all three worlds and defines success for each. It has finer vertical milestones: a walking-skeleton snake, then the tuned snake with replay, reference check and write-up, then one fish, many fish, local sight, and predator-prey, each with checkable Exit criteria and correct Depends cells. Its 12 small pipelines read clearly as call paths. Its weaknesses: routed test-planning items are still open (TC-07's direction 'to be re-derived', the TC-17 bound), the open questions repeat TC-07 with superseded wording, M2 bundles the replay viewer, reference check and write-up with the tuned DQN, and some spine packets leave out types they need (WorldSpec, EpisodeResult). Both dependency graphs are sound and mitigate edges with fakes and samples. A's better structure and closer fit to the brief edge out B's richer RL content.
